standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the relative Frobenius
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the relative Frobenius a finite morphism, so that its degree is defined.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalent characterizations of geometric reducedness
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Varieties, Lemmas lemma-geometrically-reduced-p (tag 0CC6), lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open (tag 0CCH) and lemma-generic-points-geometrically-reduced (tag 0CCE)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the three implications making up the equivalence.

core_obligations: Assemble the equivalence: (1) and (2) are equivalent by the cited Frobenius-reducedness lemma, (2) implies (3) by the dense smooth open lemma, and (3) implies (2) by geometric reducedness of the smooth locus together with the generic-point criterion (proof lines 7199-7207).
Show that under these conditions the Frobenius twist is a variety over k and the relative Frobenius is finite and dominant (remaining lines of the proof).
Compute the degree of the relative Frobenius as p^{dim(X)}, using the finiteness of the relative Frobenius and the behaviour of the function field extension, up to line 7251.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the equivalence to the three cited results.
Establish the variety structure of the Frobenius twist and finiteness/dominance of the relative Frobenius.
Compute the degree of the relative Frobenius from the function field extension.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of three conditions on a variety over a field of characteristic p - reducedness of the Frobenius twist, geometric reducedness, and the existence of a nonempty smooth open - and adds that in this case the Frobenius twist is a variety and the relative Frobenius is finite dominant of degree p^{dim(X)}. The equivalence is assembled from three cited results in the first paragraph (proof lines 7199-7207), and the substantive part is the degree computation for the relative Frobenius, which is carried out in the remainder of the proof up to line 7251 using the finiteness of the relative Frobenius and the structure of the function fields. H3: the degree p^{dim(X)} statement is the real content; the equivalence itself is a three-step citation reduction which the author writes out.
